question: Should granular `tools.fs` rules be a typed file-tool boundary with exec explicitly separate, or should OpenClaw require an OS-backed implementation that also constrains arbitrary exec before exposing the config?
rationale: Application-level path guards can mediate known file arguments, but they cannot reliably enforce every shell-mediated filesystem operation; the permanent public contract and its security claim require maintainer intent.

options.title: Ship scoped file-tool rules
options.body: Add normalized deny-wins rules under `tools.fs`, explicitly exclude host exec, and require exec denial or sandboxing for full containment.

options.title: Require OS-backed containment
options.body: Delay granular config until a sandbox backend can enforce the boundary across typed file tools and arbitrary exec.

options.title: Retain current controls
options.body: Keep `workspaceOnly`, tool denial, and Docker or OS isolation as the supported model and close the candidate implementations.

recommendation.title: Ship scoped file-tool rules
recommendation.body: Add normalized deny-wins rules under `tools.fs`, explicitly exclude host exec, and require exec denial or sandboxing for full containment.
